questions.explanation_en: On the lateral chest radiograph, the thoracic vertebrae normally look progressively more lucent (darker) as you move caudally because less soft tissue overlies them; this is the 'spine sign.' questions.explanation_en: Diverticulitis is inflammation or infection of colonic diverticula (saccular outpouchings of mucosa and submucosa through the muscular layer), most commonly in the sigmoid and descending colon; the classic presentation is left lower quadrant (LLQ) pain, fever, and altered bowel habits ('left-sided appendicitis'). Contrast-enhanced CT is the diagnostic modality of choice, with characteristic findings of colonic wall thickening (>3–4 mm), presence of diverticula, pericolic fat haziness/stranding (sign of inflammation), and in complicated cases fluid collection/abscess, free air (perforation), or fistula. questions.explanation_en: Complete opacification of one hemithorax (whiteout) on chest radiograph has three main causes, and the direction of mediastinal shift (heart, trachea, diaphragm) is the key discriminator. If the mediastinum is pushed AWAY from the opacity (shift away), the cause is increased volume: massive pleural effusion or a large mass/hernia. If the mediastinum is pulled TOWARD the opacity (shift toward), the cause is volume loss: complete lung collapse (e.g., bronchial obstruction by bronchogenic carcinoma or mucus plug) or pneumonectomy in the acute phase. questions.explanation_fa: کمخونی فقر آهن (IDA) شایعترین کمخونی جهان و شایعترین علت کمخونی میکروسیتیک هیپوکروم است. در اسمیر خون محیطی، گلبولهای قرمز کوچکتر از نرمال (میکروسیتیک، MCV پایین) و با رنگپریدگی مرکزی افزایشیافته (هیپوکروم) دیده میشوند و اغلب آنیزوسیتوز (RDW بالا) و گاه ترومبوسیتوز واکنشی (افزایش خفیف پلاکت بهدنبال خونریزی مزمن) وجود دارد. آزمایشها آهن سرم پایین، فریتین پایین (ذخایر تهی)، TIBC بالا و درصد اشباع ترانسفرین پایین را نشان میدهند. شایعترین علت در زنان سنین باروری، خونریزی مزمن قاعدگی/رحمی (مثل منوراژی ناشی از میوم رحمی) و در مردان و زنان یائسه، خونریزی مزمن دستگاه گوارش (که باید بدخیمی رد شود) است. درمان شامل جبران آهن (خوراکی فروس سولفات یا وریدی) و مهمتر از آن یافتن و رفع علت زمینهای خونریزی ا…
questions.explanation_en: Iron-deficiency anemia (IDA) is the most common anemia worldwide and the most common cause of microcytic hypochromic anemia. On the peripheral smear, red cells are smaller than normal (microcytic, low MCV) with increased central pallor (hypochromic), often with anisocytosis (high RDW) and sometimes reactive thrombocytosis (mild platelet rise following chronic bleeding). Labs show low serum iron, low ferritin (depleted stores), high TIBC, and low transferrin saturation. The most common cause in women of reproductive age is chronic menstrual/uterine bleeding (e.g., menorrhagia from uterine fibroids), and in men and postmenopausal women, chronic GI blood loss (malignancy must be excluded). questions.explanation_en: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) is the most common mesenchymal (non-epithelial) tumor of the GI tract, seen mostly in the stomach and small intestine. questions.explanation_en: Lichen planus is a T-cell–mediated inflammatory mucocutaneous disease in which cytotoxic T lymphocytes attack basal-layer keratinocytes. questions.explanation_en: Pilocytic astrocytoma is the most common primary brain tumor in children and a WHO grade 1 glioma with an excellent prognosis. Its most common site is the cerebellum, and the classic radiologic picture is a cystic mass with an enhancing mural nodule. Characteristic microscopy shows a biphasic pattern with dense areas of elongated, spindle (piloid/hair-like) glial cells and loose microcystic areas; Rosenthal fibers (twisted eosinophilic masses) and eosinophilic granular bodies are hallmarks, and mitoses and necrosis are usually absent. Microscopy now shows high-grade papillary carcinoma invading the deep muscle. questions.explanation_en: Bladder cancer (urothelial carcinoma) progresses through two distinct molecular pathways. The first is the low-grade papillary pathway, characterized by activating mutations of FGFR3 (and also RAS and PIK3CA); these tumors are usually superficial, non-invasive and papillary, and despite frequent recurrences they rarely invade muscle and have a better prognosis. The second is the high-grade/carcinoma in situ (CIS) pathway, characterized by disruption of tumor-suppressor pathways, especially TP53 mutation and loss of RB; this pathway leads to high-grade, deep muscle-invasive carcinoma and metastasis with a worse prognosis. questions.explanation_en: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is one of the most common childhood neurodevelopmental disorders, characterized by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity, and in many cases it persists into adolescence and adulthood. It is associated with a range of comorbidities and long-term outcomes, including oppositional defiant disorder and conduct disorder, learning disabilities, academic and occupational underachievement, relationship problems and low self-esteem. Most likely diagnosis? - A) Neuroleptic malignant syndrome ✅ - B) Anticholinergic toxicity - C) Acute dystonia - D) Catatonia
options_why_fa: صحیح است؛ مصرف نورولپتیک (هالوپریدول) + تب + سفتی عضلانی «سربی» + بیثباتی اتونوم + تغییر هوشیاری = سندرم نورولپتیک بدخیم (NMS)؛ پاسخ.

نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: دیستونی حاد انقباض عضلانی موضعی (تورتیکولی، کریز اکولوژیریک) بدون تب و بیثباتی اتونوم است.

questions.explanation_fa: سندرم نورولپتیک بدخیم (NMS) یک عارضهٔ نادر اما تهدیدکنندهٔ حیات ناشی از داروهای آنتاگونیست دوپامین (بهویژه آنتیسایکوتیکهای نسل اول با قدرت بالا مانند هالوپریدول) یا قطع ناگهانی داروهای دوپامینرژیک است. تظاهر بالینی کلاسیک با تتراد شامل: تب بالا، سفتی شدید عضلانی از نوع «لولهسربی» (lead-pipe rigidity)، بیثباتی اتونوم (نوسان فشار خون، تاکیکاردی، تعریق) و تغییر سطح هوشیاری (گیجی تا کوما) مشخص میشود. یافتههای آزمایشگاهی شامل افزایش شدید CPK (به دلیل رابدومیولیز)، لکوسیتوز و احتمال نارسایی کلیه از میوگلوبینوری است. questions.explanation_en: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is a rare but life-threatening complication of dopamine-antagonist drugs (especially high-potency first-generation antipsychotics such as haloperidol) or abrupt withdrawal of dopaminergic drugs. The classic presentation is a tetrad of: high fever, severe 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity, autonomic instability (fluctuating blood pressure, tachycardia, diaphoresis), and altered consciousness (confusion to coma). Laboratory findings include markedly elevated CPK (from rhabdomyolysis), leukocytosis, and possible renal failure from myoglobinuria. NMS usually develops over days after starting or increasing the dose of the drug. Important differentials include serot…

questions.explanation_en: Panic disorder is characterized by sudden, recurrent attacks of intense fear (panic attacks) in which autonomic somatic symptoms such as palpitations, shortness of breath, trembling, sweating, cold or numb extremities, chest pain, and fear of dying or going crazy peak within minutes. Between attacks, the patient develops 'anticipatory anxiety' (worry about the next attack) and behavioral change to avoid triggers. Before diagnosis, medical causes (hyperthyroidism, arrhythmia, pheochromocytoma, caffeine/stimulant use) must be excluded—in this patient the medical workup was normal. Most appropriate ER action? - A) Educate about depression and start outpatient treatment - B) Express empathy and obtain a moral commitment not to self-harm - C) Admit the patient and establish emergency safety measures ✅ - D) Refer to social work for the unemployment problem

questions.explanation_en: Assessing and managing suicide risk is one of the most important psychiatric emergencies. Assessment must weigh key components: presence of suicidal ideation, intent, a specific plan, access to means, prior attempts, degree of hopelessness, social support, and associated risk factors (depression, loss of job/loved one, being alone, substance use, male sex, chronic illness). questions.explanation_en: A halo nevus (Sutton nevus) is a mole surrounded by a round, white depigmented (pigment-free) halo. This phenomenon results from a cell-mediated immune response (cytotoxic T lymphocytes) against the melanocytes of the mole and surrounding skin, and it is common in children and adolescents and usually entirely benign; often the central mole gradually fades and disappears, and the area may later repigment. questions.explanation_en: Some skin/nail findings are markers of immunodeficiency—especially HIV/AIDS infection—and their combination has high diagnostic value. Proximal subungual onychomycosis (PSO), unlike the common distal form, begins at the proximal part of the nail and progresses as whitening and subungual hyperkeratosis; it is rare, and its presence is an important marker of immunosuppression (especially HIV). Molluscum contagiosum (shiny, pearly papules with a central umbilication), when widespread, numerous, large, or resistant in adults, points to immunodeficiency. questions.explanation_en: Acne vulgaris is common in pregnancy, and treatment choice must account for fetal safety, since many common acne drugs are contraindicated or require caution in pregnancy. Oral retinoids (isotretinoin) are highly teratogenic and absolutely contraindicated, and topical retinoids (tretinoin, adapalene category C, and tazarotene category X) are also not recommended in pregnancy. Tetracyclines (doxycycline, minocycline) are contraindicated because of effects on fetal bone growth and tooth color. questions.explanation_en: Vitiligo is an acquired autoimmune disorder in which melanocytes are destroyed, producing white, fully depigmented macules and patches with sharp margins; under a Wood's lamp these lesions appear bright white and reflective, helping distinguish them from other hypopigmented spots. Treatment is chosen based on the extent and location of lesions. In limited/localized vitiligo, first-line options are topical corticosteroids or topical calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus/pimecrolimus, especially on the face and sensitive areas) and excimer laser. questions.explanation_en: The scaphoid is the most commonly fractured carpal bone, usually following a fall on an outstretched hand (FOOSH) with pain in the anatomic snuffbox. The key point is its peculiar, vulnerable blood supply: the nutrient artery (a branch of the radial artery) enters from the distal pole and supplies the proximal pole in a retrograde (backward) fashion; therefore a fracture, especially at the proximal pole, cuts off blood flow to that part. Consequently, the common complications of scaphoid fracture are nonunion, avascular necrosis (AVN) of the proximal pole, and, in the long term, progressive wrist osteoarthritis in the SNAC wrist pattern (Scaphoid Nonunion Advanced Collapse). questions.question_en: An 8-year-old is brought to ER after severe sports injury. Severe pain and swelling at the distal tibia and fibula at the physis. X-ray shows a fracture line through the distal tibial metaphysis without displacement, but no fracture line is visible in the distal fibula. questions.explanation_en: The growth plate (physis) is a point of mechanical weakness in children, and its fractures are categorized by the Salter-Harris classification, important for both prognosis (risk of growth disturbance) and treatment. The 'SALTR' mnemonic covers five types: type I = Slipped, a fracture only across the physis without bone involvement (often no visible fracture line on radiograph, only physeal swelling/displacement); type II = Above, extending from the physis into the metaphysis (the most common type, with a Thurston-Holland metaphyseal fragment); type III = Lower, extending from the physis into the epiphysis and joint (intra-articular); type IV = Through, crossing both metaphysis and epiphysi…

questions.question_fa: پسر ۲۰ ساله ای به علت شکستگی سگمنتال استخوان تیبیا به دنبال تصادف به اورسانس مراجعه می.کنرد شرما بالفاصله جهت بیمار آتل بلند پا گرفته وice bag می گذارید. برای بیمار مسکن قوی شامل مورفین هرم تجرویز می کنید. بعد از گذشتن ۴۵ دقیقه همچنان بیمار از درد شدید ساق پا به خود می پیچد. پا و سراق بیمرار بسریار متورم است و حرکات انگشتان پا(چه اکتیو و چه پاسیو) باعث درد شدید در ساق پا می شرود. در معاینره نربض دیستال هر دو اندام پر و قرینه است وcapillary filling.انگشتان پا در حد طبیعی است اولین اقدام کره بررای این بیمار انجام می دهید چیست؟ - الف) با تشخیص سندرم کمپارتمان، بالفاصله آتل، باندکشی و ویبریل بیمار باید تا ر وی پوست باز شود و بیمار تحت نظر شما باشد. ✅ - ب) با تشخیصDVT حاد، باید سریعا تحت سونوگرافی کالر داپلر وریدی قرار گیرد. - ج) با تشخیص سندرم له (شدگیCrush Syndrome) بالفاصله به اطاق عمل منتقل شود و عمل فاشیوتومی انجام شود. - د) با تشخیص آسیب شریانی حتی با وجود نرم ال بودن نبض، سریعا بیمار تحت آنژیوگرافی شریان های پا قرار بگیرد.
questions.question_en: A 20-year-old man with a segmental tibial fracture after an accident. You immediately apply a long leg splint and ice bag and give strong analgesia (morphine). After 45 minutes he still writhes with severe leg pain. The leg/calf is very swollen and active and passive toe movement causes severe calf pain. Distal pulses are full and symmetric and toe capillary refill is normal. First action? - A) Diagnose compartment syndrome; immediately open the splint, bandage and wadding down to the skin and observe ✅ - B) Diagnose acute DVT; urgent venous color Doppler - C) Diagnose crush syndrome; immediately to OR for fasciotomy - D) Diagnose arterial injury (despite normal pulses); urgent leg angiography

questions.explanation_en: Acute compartment syndrome is an orthopedic emergency in which raised pressure within a closed fascial compartment (often after a leg fracture, especially segmental) impairs tissue perfusion and, if delayed, leads to irreversible muscle-nerve necrosis. The classic features are described by the '5 Ps,' but their timing matters: the earliest and most sensitive signs are pain out of proportion to the injury and severe pain on passive stretch of the muscles; paresthesia is the next relatively early sign; but pallor, pulselessness, and paralysis are late, ominous signs, and pulses and capillary refill may be preserved until advanced stages (so a normal pulse does not exclude compartment syndrome…

questions.question_en: A 23-year-old man had a femoral neck fracture 1 year ago fixed with three screws. He now presents with pain disrupting his life. X-ray shows non-union of the fracture with avascular necrosis of the femoral head and degenerative changes. Best treatment? - A) Total hip replacement ✅ - B) Re-fixation of the femoral neck - C) Re-fixation with bone grafting - D) Drilling of head and neck with re-fixation and bone grafting
options_fa: ثابت کردن مجدد شکستگی گردن ران

questions.explanation_fa: پای چماقی مادرزادی (کلابفوت یا talipes equinovarus) یک دفورمیتی شایع مادرزادی پا است که با چهار جزء مشخص میشود که با کمکحافظهٔ «CAVE» به یاد میآیند: Cavus (قوس کف پا افزایشیافته)، Adductus (اداکشن متاتارسها و انگشتان به داخل)، Varus (واروس پاشنه) و Equinus (اکینوس مچ پا/پلانتار فلکشن). میتواند ایزوله (ایدیوپاتیک) یا همراه با سندرمها/اختلالات عصبی-عضلانی باشد؛ در نوزاد با سایر معاینات طبیعی، فرم ایدیوپاتیک مطرح است. درمان استاندارد و خط اول، روش پونستی (Ponseti) است که شامل گچگیریهای سریال هفتگی از همان روزهای اول تولد برای اصلاح تدریجی اجزای دفورمیتی به ترتیب (ابتدا کاووس، سپس اداکتوس و واروس، و در آخر اکینوس)، معمولاً بههمراه تنوتومی پوستی تاندون آشیل برای اصلاح اکینوس، و سپس استفادهٔ طولا…
questions.explanation_en: Congenital clubfoot (talipes equinovarus) is a common congenital foot deformity characterized by four components remembered with the 'CAVE' mnemonic: Cavus (increased plantar arch), Adductus (adduction of the metatarsals and toes inward), Varus (heel varus), and Equinus (ankle equinus/plantarflexion). It may be isolated (idiopathic) or associated with syndromes/neuromuscular disorders; in a neonate with otherwise normal examination, the idiopathic form is likely. questions.explanation_en: Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is a common cause of groin (inguinal) pain in young people and athletes, resulting from abnormal repetitive contact between the femoral head/neck and the acetabular rim. It has two main types: Cam (a bony prominence at the head-neck junction) and Pincer (over-coverage of the acetabulum over the femoral head), often seen together (mixed), and can lead to labral injury and early hip osteoarthritis. The classic presentation is dull groin pain aggravated by prolonged sitting, activity, and rising from a car; the characteristic diagnostic test is FADIR (hip Flexion + ADduction + Internal Rotation), which reproduces the pain. questions.explanation_en: Adhesive capsulitis, or 'frozen shoulder,' is a painful shoulder disorder characterized by inflammation and progressive fibrosis of the glenohumeral joint capsule with adhesions, leading to movement restriction. The most important risk factor is diabetes (higher prevalence and severity), and other factors include thyroid disorders, prolonged immobilization, and age 40–60 with female sex. questions.explanation_en: Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC; including Ta, T1, and carcinoma in situ/CIS) is often completed after transurethral resection of the tumor (TURBT) with intravesical therapy to reduce the risk of recurrence and progression. There are two main categories of intravesical therapy: (1) intravesical chemotherapy (such as mitomycin C or gemcitabine), which mainly reduces tumor 'recurrence' but has no proven effect on preventing 'progression' to muscle-invasive disease; and (2) immunotherapy with BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guérin), which triggers a local immune response against tumor cells. questions.explanation_en: A urethral diverticulum is a saccular outpouching of the urethra into the surrounding tissue, seen mostly in women and usually arising from obstruction and infection of the periurethral glands. Its classic presentation is described by the '3 Ds': Dysuria (burning on urination), Dyspareunia (pain during intercourse), and post-void Dribbling; on examination, a tender or painful mass is palpable in the anterior vaginal wall that on pressure may express purulent discharge or urine. Diagnosis is confirmed by pelvic MRI (method of choice), cystourethroscopy, or urography. The definitive treatment is surgical excision of the diverticulum (diverticulectomy) or marsupialization. questions.explanation_en: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is a retinal vascular disorder in premature infants in which abnormal retinal vessel growth can lead to neovascularization, retinal detachment, and blindness; the main risk factors are severe prematurity, low birth weight, and prolonged/uncontrolled oxygen therapy. ROP screening is recommended for infants with gestational age ≤30 weeks or birth weight ≤1500 g (and larger infants with an unstable clinical course at the neonatologist's discretion). questions.explanation_fa: گلوکوم مادرزادی اولیه (primary congenital glaucoma) یک بیماری نادر اما اورژانسی چشمی در شیرخواران است که از رشد ناقص زاویهٔ اتاق قدامی (ترابکولودیسژنزی) و اختلال تخلیهٔ زلالیه و افزایش فشار داخلچشم ناشی میشود. سهگانهٔ کلاسیک علائم عبارتاند از اپیفورا (اشکریزش مداوم)، فتوفوبی (ترس از نور) و بلفاروسپاسم (بستن مکرر و اسپاسم پلکها). به دلیل انعطافپذیری اسکلرا و قرنیه در شیرخوار، فشار بالا باعث بزرگشدن کرهٔ چشم و قرنیه (بوفتالموس/مگالوکورنه)، کدورت قرنیه و پارگیهای غشای دسمه بهشکل خطوط متحدالمرکز افقی به نام خطوط Haab میشود که مشخصهٔ بیماری است. افتراق مهم: انسداد مجرای نازولاکریمال هم اشکریزش میدهد اما قرنیهٔ بزرگ، فتوفوبی و Haab ندارد؛ کراتیت هرپسی کدورت و قرمزی میدهد اما بوفتالموس ایجاد نمیکند…
questions.explanation_en: Primary congenital glaucoma is a rare but ophthalmic-emergency disease in infants, arising from incomplete development of the anterior chamber angle (trabeculodysgenesis) with impaired aqueous drainage and raised intraocular pressure. The classic triad of symptoms is epiphora (persistent tearing), photophobia (light sensitivity), and blepharospasm (frequent eyelid closure/spasm). Because the infant's sclera and cornea are elastic, high pressure causes enlargement of the eyeball and cornea (buphthalmos/megalocornea), corneal clouding, and breaks in Descemet's membrane appearing as horizontal concentric lines called Haab striae, which are characteristic. questions.explanation_en: Vernal keratoconjunctivitis (VKC) is a chronic, bilateral allergic inflammation of the conjunctiva and cornea that mainly affects boys in childhood and adolescence, with symptoms exacerbated in spring/warm seasons. Features include intense itching, tearing, sticky mucoid discharge, photophobia, and a foreign-body sensation. On examination, two forms are seen: a tarsal form with giant 'cobblestone' papillae on the upper tarsus (eyelid), and a limbal form with limbal hypertrophy and white eosinophilic dots called Horner-Trantas dots. The most vision-threatening complication is corneal involvement (shield ulcer). Treatment is stepwise: allergen avoidance and cold compresses, artificial tears,…

questions.explanation_en: Orbital cellulitis is a bacterial infection of the soft tissues behind the orbital septum (inside the orbit) and an ophthalmic-infectious emergency, occurring mostly in children and often secondary to sinusitis (especially ethmoid). Distinguishing it from preseptal (pre-septal) cellulitis is critical: in preseptal cellulitis there is only eyelid swelling and redness with normal eye movement, vision, and globe position; but in orbital cellulitis, in addition to eyelid swelling, signs of intraorbital involvement appear: painful and restricted eye movement (ophthalmoplegia), proptosis (bulging eye), chemosis (conjunctival edema), and decreased vision and color-vision impairment, which indicate…

questions.explanation_en: The trochlear nerve (cranial nerve four, CN4) innervates the superior oblique muscle; this muscle's actions are intorsion (inward rotation of the globe), depression (lowering the eye especially in adduction), and abduction. The key point is that the fourth nerve, due to its peculiar anatomy—the longest intracranial course among the ocular motor nerves, emergence from the dorsal surface of the brainstem and wrapping around it, and passage near the tentorium cerebelli—is highly vulnerable to head trauma, and the most common cause of isolated fourth nerve palsy is head trauma. questions.explanation_en: Abnormal breathing sounds are classified by the level of airway obstruction, and recognizing them is key to localizing the obstruction and managing the airway emergently. By contrast, 'stridor' is a high-pitched sound from obstruction at the larynx or trachea, and its pattern localizes the obstruction: inspiratory stridor usually indicates supraglottic/glottic obstruction; expiratory stridor points more to intrathoraci…

questions.explanation_fa: آپنهٔ انسدادی خواب (Obstructive Sleep Apnea = OSA) از کلاپس مکرر راه هوایی فوقانی حین خواب ناشی میشود و میتواند در چند سطح رخ دهد: کام نرم و اووولا (ولوفارنکس)، دیوارهٔ جانبی اوروفارنکس و لوزهها، قاعدهٔ زبان، و اپیگلوت. تشخیص قطعی OSA با پلیسومنوگرافی (سنجش AHI) گذاشته میشود، اما برای انتخاب درمان جراحی هدفمند لازم است محل دقیق و الگوی کلاپس تعیین شود. روشهای بیداری مانند معاینهٔ کرانیوفاسیال، نمرهٔ مالامپاتی و مانور مولر (نازوفارنگوسکوپی فیبراپتیک همراه با تلاش دمی در برابر راه هوایی بسته) محدودیت دارند، زیرا وضعیت پویا و شلشدن عضلات حین خواب واقعی را بازتاب نمیدهند و همبستگی ضعیفی با انسداد حقیقی دارند. آندوسکوپی خواب القاشده با دارو (Drug-Induced Sleep Endoscopy = DISE) با ایجاد خواب دار…
questions.explanation_en: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) results from repetitive collapse of the upper airway during sleep and can occur at several levels: the soft palate and uvula (velopharynx), the lateral oropharyngeal walls and tonsils, the tongue base, and the epiglottis. Definitive diagnosis of OSA is made by polysomnography (measuring the AHI), but for selecting targeted surgical treatment the exact site and pattern of collapse must be determined. questions.explanation_en: Benign lymphoepithelial lesions/cysts (BLEL) are multiple, often bilateral cysts of the parotid salivary gland, seen on ultrasound/imaging as multiple small cysts with parotid enlargement. The most important clinical point is that multiple, bilateral parotid lymphoepithelial cysts are a well-recognized and relatively specific manifestation of HIV infection (especially in early stages or as an initial presentation), arising from intraglandular lymphoid hyperplasia. Therefore, in a patient (especially young) who presents with this finding, the next and decisive step is HIV screening; even without other symptoms, this finding should raise underlying HIV infection. questions.explanation_en: Nasal bone fracture is the most common facial fracture and often occurs after direct trauma (such as a punch), possibly with lateral displacement or depression (a C-shaped deformity). questions.explanation_en: Esophageal cancer is an important health problem in Iran, and its epidemiologic pattern has distinctive features. Iran is part of the 'Asian esophageal cancer belt,' and the highest incidence is in the northern and northeastern provinces (especially Golestan, Mazandaran, Ardabil), not the southern provinces. The predominant histologic type in Iran is squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), whereas in developed Western countries adenocarcinoma (linked to reflux, Barrett esophagus, and obesity) has become predominant in recent decades; thus the cancer-type pattern in Iran differs from developed countries. questions.explanation_en: Herd immunity (community immunity) is a fundamental epidemiologic concept and the basis of vaccination programs. questions.explanation_en: Social health is one of the four dimensions of health, alongside physical, mental, and spiritual health, and refers to the quality of a person's relationships, participation, and functioning in society, as well as the social conditions that affect health. Contrary to a common misconception, social health is not merely a community-level concept but is defined and measured at both the individual and collective levels. questions.explanation_en: Colchicine is an old, effective anti-inflammatory drug in gout with a unique mechanism of action: by binding to the protein tubulin, it prevents its polymerization and the formation of microtubules. questions.explanation_en: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs; such as phenelzine, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid) are a class of older antidepressants that, by inhibiting the enzyme monoamine oxidase, reduce the breakdown of monoamine neurotransmitters (serotonin, norepinephrine, dopamine) and increase their levels. A dangerous, classic interaction of these drugs is the 'tyramine reaction' or 'cheese reaction': tyramine is an amine found in fermented, aged, and ripe foods (aged cheeses, red wine, beer, sausages and cured meats, soy, fermented products) that is normally broken down in the gut and liver by MAO. questions.explanation_en: Triage in intensive and critical care is the ethical and scientific process of allocating scarce resources (such as an ICU bed, ventilator, medication) when demand exceeds supply (as in a mass-casualty incident). The ethical principles governing crisis triage are based on a combination of utility and equity/justice; the main goal is 'maximizing benefit'—that is, saving the greatest number of lives or life-years—by allocating resources to patients with the greatest likelihood of benefiting and surviving with treatment, based on objective scientific and clinical criteria (severity of illness, likelihood of response to treatment, prognosis). This decision must be fair, transparent, consistent,…

questions.explanation_en: Informed consent is one of the fundamental pillars of medical ethics, based on the principle of respect for patient autonomy. Valid informed consent has four essential elements: (1) disclosure of sufficient information: the physician must clearly explain to the patient the diagnosis, the nature and purpose of the proposed treatment/procedure, potential risks and complications, alternative treatment methods, and the consequences of no treatment or the possibility of failure; (2) comprehension: the patient must understand the information, and the physician should ensure this understanding; (3) voluntariness: the decision must be made voluntarily, without coercion, deception, or pressure; and…

questions.explanation_en: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) are the cornerstone of controller therapy for chronic pediatric asthma, reducing airway inflammation and preventing exacerbations; however, long-term use—especially at medium-to-high doses—has local and systemic effects that mandate regular monitoring. Local effects: oropharyngeal candidiasis (thrush) and dysphonia (hoarseness), reduced by using a spacer, and rinsing/gargling the mouth after each inhalation. questions.question_fa: کودک7 سالهای از حدود 3 ماه قبل دچار دیابت شیرین شده است و در حال حاضر تحت درمان انسولین با دوز و فواصل مناسب قرار دارد. وی به دلیل افتهای مکرر قند خون به اورژانس آورده شده است. در شرح حال و معاینه بالینی نکته غیرطبیعی ندارد. محتملترین تشخیص چیست؟
questions.question_en: A 7-year-old diagnosed with diabetes 3 months ago, on appropriately dosed insulin, presents with recurrent hypoglycemia. History and exam are unremarkable. Most likely diagnosis?
options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: در این مورد، پاسخ صحیح «مرحله ماه عسل» است زیرا: مرحلهٔ ماهعسل (honeymoon phase / partial remission) در دیابت نوع ۱ پدیدهای شایع و مهم است که معمولاً هفتهها تا چند ماه پس از شروع انسولیندرمانی و برطرفشدن سمیت گلوکز (glucotoxicity) آغاز میشود. در این مرحله، سلولهای بتای پانکراس که هنوز بهطور کامل تخریب نشدهاند، عملکرد ترشحی خود را بهطور موقت بازمییابند و انسولین اندوژن ترشح میکنند؛ در نتیجه نیاز به انسولین اگزوژن بهشدت کاهش مییابد (اغلب به کمتر از ۰٫۵ واحد/کیلوگرم/روز) و کنترل قند با دوزهای «بهظاهر مناسب» منجر به هیپوگلیسمیهای مکرر میشود. تشخیص این مرحله بالینی است: کودکی که چند ماه پس از تشخیص دیابت نوع ۱، با دوز استاندارد انسولین دچار افتقندهای تکراری میشود. نکات کلیدی مدیریت: (۱) کاهش تدریجی دوز انسولین برای پیشگیری از هیپوگلیسمی، نه قط…

questions.explanation_en: The honeymoon phase (partial remission) of type 1 diabetes is a common, important phenomenon that usually begins weeks to a few months after starting insulin and resolution of glucotoxicity. In this phase, pancreatic beta cells that are not yet fully destroyed temporarily recover their secretory function and produce endogenous insulin; consequently, exogenous insulin requirements fall sharply (often to <0.5 U/kg/day), and glycemic control with 'seemingly appropriate' doses leads to recurrent hypoglycemia. options_fa: تزریق واکسن توام بزرگسالTd) + ایمونوگلوبولین ضدکزازTIG)
options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: در این مورد، پاسخ صحیح «تزریق واکسن توام بزرگسال Td)» است زیرا: پیشگیری از کزاز پس از زخم بر دو محور استوار است: وضعیت واکسیناسیون فرد و ماهیت زخم (تمیز-جزئی در برابر مستعد کزاز). زخمهای مستعد کزاز شامل زخمهای عمیق، آلوده به خاک/بزاق، گازگرفتگی، لهشدگی، سوختگی و زخمهای نکروتیکاند. در فردی که واکسیناسیون کامل (سه دوز یا بیشتر) دارد: برای زخم تمیز-جزئی تنها اگر ≥۱۰ سال از آخرین دوز گذشته باشد بوستر Td لازم است؛ برای زخم مستعد کزاز اگر ≥۵ سال گذشته باشد یک دوز بوستر Td تجویز میشود. ایمونوگلوبولین ضدکزاز (TIG) فقط زمانی افزوده میشود که واکسیناسیون ناقص یا نامشخص باشد یا فرد نقص ایمنی داشته باشد. بنابراین در این پسر با واکسیناسیون کامل و زخم مستعد کزاز، اقدام درست تجویز بوستر Td (در صورت فاصلهٔ ≥۵ سال) بدون TIG است. شستوشو و دبریدمان زخم و در گازگرفتگی، پروف…

questions.explanation_en: Post-wound tetanus prophylaxis rests on two axes: the patient's vaccination status and the wound's nature (clean-minor vs tetanus-prone). Tetanus-prone wounds include deep, soil/saliva-contaminated, bite, crush, burn and necrotic wounds. In a fully vaccinated person (≥3 doses): for a clean-minor wound a Td booster is needed only if ≥10 years since the last dose; for a tetanus-prone wound a single Td booster is given if ≥5 years have elapsed. Tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG) is added only when vaccination is incomplete/unknown or the person is immunodeficient. options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: در این مورد، پاسخ صحیح «گرافی قفسه سینه — _Chest X-ray_» است زیرا: بلع مواد خورنده (corrosive/caustic ingestion) در کودکان یک اورژانس شایع است؛ عوامل شامل مواد قلیایی (شویندهها، بازکنندهٔ لوله، شیشهپاککن) و اسیدی (جرمگیر) هستند. قلیاها با نکروز مایعکننده (liquefactive) نفوذ عمقی و آسیب مری، و اسیدها با نکروز انعقادی (coagulative) بیشتر آسیب معده ایجاد میکنند. اقدامات ممنوع و خطرناک: القای استفراغ (تماس مجدد مخاط با ماده و خطر آسپیراسیون)، شستوشوی معده/لاواژ، تجویز زغال فعال (به آندوسکوپی تصویری دید نمیدهد و بیاثر است) و خنثیسازی کور با اسید/باز (واکنش گرمازا و آسیب بیشتر). اقدامات اولیهٔ صحیح: ارزیابی و حفظ راه هوایی (خطر ادم و انسداد)، NPO کردن بیمار، مایعدرمانی وریدی، کنترل درد، و ارزیابی علائم خطر (استریدور، دیسترس تنفسی، سوراخشدگی). ارکان تشخیص و پیشآگ…

questions.explanation_en: Corrosive/caustic ingestion in children is a common emergency; agents include alkalis (detergents, drain cleaner, glass cleaner) and acids (descalers). Alkalis cause deep-penetrating liquefactive necrosis and esophageal injury, whereas acids cause coagulative necrosis with more gastric injury. Prohibited, dangerous actions: inducing vomiting (re-exposes mucosa and risks aspiration), gastric lavage, activated charcoal (useless and obscures endoscopic view), and blind neutralization with acid/base (exothermic reaction causing more injury). Correct initial measures: assess and protect the airway (risk of edema and obstruction), keep the patient NPO, give IV fluids, control pain, and assess red…

questions.question_fa: شیرخوار یک ساله با حال عمومی خوب و وزنگیری مطلوب به دلیل رنگپریدگی ویزیت میشود. شیرخوار به طور عمده با شیر خشک تغذیه میشود و تمایل کمی به غذای کمکی دارد. در معاینه فقط رنگپریدگی دارد. هموگلوبین 9 میلیگرم در دسیلیتر است. گلبولهای قرمز در گستره خون محیطی کوچکتر و کمرنگتر از طبیعی هستند. با توجه به محتملترین تشخیص، بهترین اقدام تشخیصی در این شیرخوار کدام است؟

Exam shows only pallor. Hb 9 g/dL; peripheral smear shows small, pale RBCs. Given the most likely diagnosis, what is the best diagnostic step?

questions.explanation_en: Iron-deficiency anemia is the commonest anemia of infancy, peaking at 9–24 months, especially in infants fed mainly on milk (excess cow's milk or heavy formula dependence) with low intake of iron-rich complementary foods. The laboratory picture is microcytic-hypochromic anemia (low MCV, high RDW). In a well-appearing infant with good growth, a perfectly matching dietary history, and a microcytic-hypochromic smear, iron deficiency is most likely, and the standard cost-effective approach is a therapeutic trial of oral iron (~3–6 mg/kg/day elemental iron). The expected response is a reticulocytosis within 5–7 days and a rise in hemoglobin of ~1 g/dL over 2–4 weeks, which confirms the diagnosis…

questions.explanation_en: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is the most common lethal autosomal recessive disease in Caucasians, caused by mutations in the CFTR gene (chromosome 7; the commonest mutation is ΔF508). CFTR is a chloride channel; its defect produces thick, viscous secretions in the epithelia of the airways, pancreas, intestine, liver, and reproductive tract. Multisystem manifestations: (1) respiratory—recurrent infections (Staphylococcus aureus in childhood, then Pseudomonas aeruginosa), chronic cough, bronchiectasis, and ultimately respiratory failure; (2) gastrointestinal—neonatal meconium ileus (nearly pathognomonic), exocrine pancreatic insufficiency with fat malabsorption, steatorrhea and failure to thrive, def…

questions.question_en: While assessing a child's breathing you note a cyclic pattern of waxing and waning depth interrupted by periods of apnea. Given this pattern, which is suggested?

questions.explanation_en: Cheyne-Stokes respiration is a cyclic pattern in which breathing depth gradually increases (crescendo) then decreases (decrescendo), ending in a period of apnea, with the cycle repeating. The mechanism involves a delayed feedback loop in respiratory control and oscillating sensitivity of the respiratory center to carbon dioxide. Key causes include congestive heart failure (low output and prolonged circulation time), bilateral cerebral hemisphere or upper brainstem lesions, and metabolic disturbances such as uremia. options_fa: نقص چسبندگی لکوسیت نوع اول — _Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1_
options_why_fa: صحیح است؛ نقص چسبندگی لکوسیت نوع ۱ (Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency type 1, LAD-1) یک نقص ایمنی اولیهٔ اتوزومال مغلوب ناشی از جهش در ژن ITGB2 است که زیرواحد مشترک β2-اینتگرین (CD18) را کد میکند. این زیرواحد در ساخت مولکولهای چسبندگی نوتروفیل (LFA-1/CD11a، Mac-1/CD11b) نقش دارد؛ نبود آن مانع چسبندگی محکم نوتروفیل به اندوتلیوم، مهاجرت ترانساندوتلیال (دیاپدز) و رسیدن به محل عفونت میشود—در نتیجه نوتروفیلها در خون تجمع مییابند اما به بافت نمیرسند. تظاهرات کلاسیک: (۱) تأخیر جداشدن بند ناف (بیش از ۳ هفته؛ اُمفالیت)؛ نشانهٔ شاخص و پرسششونده در امتحان؛ (۲) عفونتهای باکتریایی و قارچی مکرر و شدید پوست، مخاط و بافتهای نرم بدون تشکیل چرک (چون نوتروفیل به محل نمیرسد)؛ (۳) زخمهای پوستی/مخاطی با بهبود ضعیف و بدون ترشح…

questions.explanation_en: Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency type 1 (LAD-1) is an autosomal recessive primary immunodeficiency caused by mutations in ITGB2, which encodes the common β2-integrin subunit (CD18). This subunit is required to build neutrophil adhesion molecules (LFA-1/CD11a, Mac-1/CD11b); its absence prevents firm neutrophil adhesion to endothelium, transendothelial migration (diapedesis), and arrival at sites of infection—so neutrophils accumulate in blood but fail to reach tissue. options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: در این مورد، پاسخ صحیح «پروفیلاکسی با آنتیبیوتیک خوراکی» است زیرا: بیماری مننگوکوکی (نایسریا مننژایتیدیس، دیپلوکوک گرممنفی): میتواند به صورت مننژیت و/یا مننگوکوکسمی برقآسا با پورپورای غیربلانچینگ، شوک و DIC تظاهر کند. پروفیلاکسی پس از مواجهه برای تماسهای نزدیک (همخانه، تماس با ترشحات تنفسی، مهدکودک) ضروری است: ریفامپین، سیپروفلوکساسین یا سفتریاکسون، هرچه زودتر (ترجیحاً ظرف ۲۴ ساعت). واکسیناسیون در طغیانهای سروگروپ خاص و گروههای پرخطر توصیه میشود؛ گزارش فوری به نظام بهداشت الزامی است.

questions.explanation_en: Meningococcal disease (Neisseria meningitidis, gram-negative diplococcus): may present as meningitis and/or fulminant meningococcemia with non-blanching purpura, shock and DIC. Post-exposure prophylaxis for close contacts (household, respiratory-secretion contact, daycare) is essential: rifampin, ciprofloxacin or ceftriaxone, as early as possible (ideally within 24 h). Vaccination is advised in serogroup-specific outbreaks and high-risk groups; mandatory prompt public-health reporting.

questions.explanation_en: Bronchiolitis is the most common lower respiratory tract infection in infants under 2 years (peak 2–6 months), most often caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV); other agents include rhinovirus, metapneumovirus, and parainfluenza. Pathophysiology: inflammation and edema of the bronchiolar epithelium, increased mucus secretion, and cellular necrosis obstruct small airways, causing air trapping (hyperinflation), ventilation-perfusion mismatch, and hypoxia. Clinical presentation: a few-day coryzal prodrome (rhinorrhea, cough, low-grade fever) followed by tachypnea, wheezing and diffuse crackles, retractions, and apnea in young infants. questions.explanation_en: Pediatric septic arthritis: a joint emergency with fever, pain, restricted movement and purulent synovial fluid. The commonest organism at all ages is Staphylococcus aureus; in infants Kingella kingae (gram-negative) is also considered, and in sexually active adolescents Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Synovial-fluid Gram stain guides empiric therapy: gram-positive cocci → anti-staph cover (nafcillin/oxacillin, or vancomycin where MRSA is prevalent). Joint drainage alongside antibiotics is essential.

options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: در این مورد، پاسخ صحیح «بیماری کرون» است زیرا: بیماری التهابی روده (IBD) شامل بیماری کرون و کولیت اولسراتیو در کودکان و نوجوانان اهمیت زیادی دارد و اغلب با تأخیر رشد و بلوغ تظاهر میکند. بیماری کرون میتواند هر بخش از دستگاه گوارش از دهان تا مقعد را درگیر کند، ضایعات آن قطعهقطعه (skip lesions) و تمامضخامت (transmural) است و میتواند با فیستول، تنگی و آبسه همراه شود. تظاهرات بالینی شامل درد شکم مزمن، اسهال (گاه خونی)، بیاشتهایی، کاهش وزن و عقبماندگی رشد است. تظاهرات بیرونرودهای مهماند و گاه اولین سرنخاند: اریتم ندوزوم (ندولهای دردناک قرمز-بنفش روی ساق)، آرتریت/آرترالژی، یووئیت، پیودرما گانگرنوزوم، استوماتیت آفتی و کلانژیت اسکلروزان اولیه. وجود اریتم ندوزوم در کنار اسهال خونی مزمن و کاهش وزن، احتمال کرون را بسیار بالا میبرد. تشخیص با کالپروت…

questions.explanation_en: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) — Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis — is important in children and adolescents and often presents with growth and pubertal delay. Crohn disease can involve any part of the GI tract from mouth to anus, with segmental (skip) lesions and transmural involvement, and may be complicated by fistulae, strictures and abscesses. Clinical features include chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea (sometimes bloody), anorexia, weight loss and growth failure. questions.question_fa: کودک5 ساله با شکایت تب و اسهال خونی از5 روز مراجعه کرده است. بیمار سفکسیم دریافت کرده است. در معاینه رنگ پریدگی دارد و فشارخون 55/80 میباشد. بیمار بستری میشود. برونده ادراری 3 میلیلیتر بر کیلوگرم در ساعت است. گستره خون محیطی نشانگر شیستوسایت است. با توجه به آزمایشهای زیر اقدام مناسب کدام است؟ Hb= 5 gr/dl, PLT.= 30.000/µL, BUN= 70 mg/dl, Creat.= 2 mg/dl
questions.question_en: A 5-year-old presents with 5 days of fever and bloody diarrhea and has received cefixime. On exam pale, BP 80/55; admitted. Urine output 3 mL/kg/hr. Peripheral smear shows schistocytes. Given Hb 5 g/dL, PLT 30,000/µL, BUN 70 mg/dL, Cr 2 mg/dL, the appropriate action is:

questions.explanation_en: Hemolytic-uremic syndrome (HUS) is the commonest cause of acute kidney injury in young children, and its typical form (D+ HUS) follows bloody diarrhea due to Shiga-toxin-producing E. coli (O157:H7) or Shigella. The classic triad is microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (schistocytes on smear), thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury. Treatment is chiefly supportive: meticulous fluid and electrolyte management, blood pressure control, red-cell transfusion for symptomatic anemia, and avoidance of routine platelet transfusion unless active bleeding or an invasive procedure is needed. Antibiotics are generally not recommended in Shiga-toxin-associated HUS because they may increase toxin release a…

questions.question_fa: دختر10 سالهای از دوهفته قبل بدون سابقه قبلی دچار زردی پیشرونده شده است. در معاینه ایکتر دارد و نقاط اکیموز روی بدن مشاهده میشود. کبد چهار سانتیمتر زیر لبه دنده در خط وسط کلاویکول لمس میشود. اخیرا مقداری خوابآلودگی و گیجی پیدا کرده است. سایر معاینات طبیعی هستند. محتملترین تشخیص کدام است؟
questions.question_en: A 10-year-old girl has 2 weeks of progressive jaundice with no prior history. Exam shows icterus and ecchymoses; the liver is palpable 4 cm below the costal margin at the midclavicular line. She has recently become somewhat drowsy and confused. Other exams are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: در این مورد، پاسخ صحیح «هپاتیت فولمینانت» است زیرا: نارسایی حاد کبدی (فولمینانت) در کودکان به صورت بروز اختلال شدید عملکرد کبد همراه با کوآگولوپاتی (INR بالا که با ویتامین K اصلاح نمیشود) و انسفالوپاتی کبدی، در فردی بدون بیماری کبدی مزمنِ شناختهشده، طی هفتهها تعریف میشود. علل شایع شامل هپاتیتهای ویروسی (بهویژه A و B و در برخی نواحی E)، مسمومیت دارویی (استامینوفن)، بیماریهای متابولیک (بیماری ویلسون در کودکان بزرگتر)، هپاتیت خودایمن و علل ایسکمیک است. تظاهرات بالینی شامل یرقان پیشرونده، خونریزی و اکیموز به دلیل کاهش سنتز فاکتورهای انعقادی، و تغییرات نورولوژیک (خوابآلودگی، گیجی، آسترکسیس تا کوما) است. یافتهٔ کلیدی افتراقی، وجود همزمان انسفالوپاتی و کوآگولوپاتی است که این حالت را از هپاتیت ساده جدا میکند. این وضعیت اورژانس پزشکی است؛ اداره در بخش…

questions.explanation_en: Acute (fulminant) liver failure in children is defined as severe hepatic dysfunction with coagulopathy (elevated INR not corrected by vitamin K) and hepatic encephalopathy, developing over weeks in a person without known chronic liver disease. Common causes include viral hepatitis (especially A and B, and E in some regions), drug toxicity (acetaminophen), metabolic disease (Wilson disease in older children), autoimmune hepatitis, and ischemic causes. Clinical features include progressive jaundice, bleeding and ecchymoses from reduced synthesis of clotting factors, and neurologic changes (drowsiness, confusion, asterixis up to coma). questions.question_fa: شیرخوار یک سالهای به علت بیحالی و بیاشتهایی مورد بررسی قرار گرفته است. در شرح حال و معاینه انجام شده، تغذیه عمدتا با شیر گاو بوده است. در معاینه فاقد ارگانومگالی میباشد. در آزمایشات انجام شده: Hb= 8 gr/dl, Retic.= 1% در لام خون محیطی گلبولهای قرمز هیپوکرومیک و میکروسیتیک هستند. بیمار تحت درمان آزمایشی قرار گرفته و سه روز بعد مجددا ارزیابی میگردد. انتظار میرود کدامیک از پارامترهای زیر افزایش یافته باشد؟

questions.explanation_en: Iron-deficiency anemia is the most common anemia of infancy and childhood; its classic cause in infants is excessive cow's milk intake. Cow's milk is both low in and low in bioavailable iron and worsens iron deficiency by provoking chronic occult gastrointestinal bleeding and reducing iron absorption (recommendation: avoid whole cow's milk before 12 months and limit to <500 mL/day thereafter). Pathophysiology: falling iron stores first lower ferritin, then serum iron and transferrin saturation drop while TIBC rises, and finally impaired hemoglobin synthesis produces a hypochromic microcytic anemia with high RDW and a peripheral smear of small, pale red cells. Presentation: pallor, lethargy,…

options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: در این مورد، پاسخ صحیح «تجویز مانیتول وریدی زنان و زایمان» است زیرا: ادم مغزی، خطرناکترین و کشندهترین عارضهٔ کتواسیدوز دیابتی (DKA) بهویژه در کودکان است و علت اصلی مرگومیر DKA کودکان محسوب میشود. معمولاً ۴–۱۲ ساعت پس از شروع درمان بروز میکند (اما میتواند پیش از درمان یا دیرتر هم رخ دهد). پاتوفیزیولوژی چندعاملی است و شامل تغییرات اسمولاریته، ایسکمی-ریپرفیوژن و اختلال در انتقال یونها در سد خونی-مغزی میشود. عوامل خطر شناختهشده: سن کمتر، DKA شدید و طولانی، افت سریع اسمولالیته و قند خون، مایعدرمانی حجیم و سریع در ساعات اول، تجویز بیکربنات، و عدم افزایش سدیم اصلاحشده حین درمان. تظاهر بالینی (باید فعالانه پایش شود): سردرد (اغلب اولین نشانه)، افت سطح هوشیاری، تغییر رفتار، استفراغ مکرر، برادیکاردی و افزایش فشارخون (پاسخ کوشینگ)، بیاختیاری، فلج اعصاب مغزی و ادم پاپی.…

questions.explanation_en: Cerebral edema is the most dangerous and lethal complication of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), especially in children, and is the leading cause of DKA-related death in children. It usually occurs 4–12 hours after starting treatment (but can occur before treatment or later). The pathophysiology is multifactorial, involving changes in osmolality, ischemia-reperfusion, and disrupted ion transport at the blood-brain barrier. Recognized risk factors: younger age, severe and prolonged DKA, rapid falls in osmolality and glucose, large and rapid fluid administration in the early hours, bicarbonate administration, and failure of corrected sodium to rise during treatment. questions.explanation_en: A hemorrhagic ovarian cyst and its rupture are a common cause of acute pelvic pain in reproductive-age women, often occurring in the luteal phase (after ovulation, from a corpus luteum cyst). Pathophysiology: bleeding within a follicular or corpus luteum cyst and, on rupture, spillage of blood into the peritoneal cavity causing sudden pain and peritoneal signs. Evaluation: history (relation to the luteal phase, sudden onset, sometimes after exertion or intercourse), examination, a pregnancy test (βhCG) to exclude ectopic pregnancy—the most important dangerous differential—and transvaginal ultrasound (cyst with internal echoes/clot, free fluid in the cul-de-sac). questions.question_en: All of the following are recommended to assess ovulation in an infertile couple EXCEPT:

options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: در این مورد، پاسخ صحیح «بیوپسی اندومتر جهت بررسی هیستولوژیک» است زیرا: ارزیابی تخمکگذاری بخش پایهای بررسی زوج نابارور است، زیرا اختلالات تخمکگذاری یکی از شایعترین علل ناباروری زنانهاند. روشهای معتبر و توصیهشدهٔ تأیید تخمکگذاری: (۱) اندازهگیری پروژسترون سرم در وسط فاز لوتئال (روز ۲۱ در چرخهٔ ۲۸ روزه یا ۷ روز پیش از قاعدگی مورد انتظار)؛ سطح >۳ ng/mL مؤید وقوع تخمکگذاری است—این حساسترین و عملیترین آزمون است؛ (۲) کیتهای ادراری پیشبینی تخمکگذاری (OPK) که موج LH پیش از تخمکگذاری را شناسایی میکنند؛ (۳) نمودار دمای پایهٔ بدن (BBT) که افزایش حدود ۰٫۳–۰٫۵ درجهٔ سانتیگراد پس از تخمکگذاری (اثر ترموژنیک پروژسترون) را نشان میدهد—ارزان اما گذشتهنگر و کمدقت؛ (۴) پایش سونوگرافیک رشد فولیکول و فروپاشی آن؛ (۵) سابقهٔ قاعدگی منظم که خود شاهدی قوی بر تخمکگذاری است. آزمونی که دیگر…

questions.explanation_en: Assessing ovulation is a fundamental part of the infertile-couple workup, since ovulatory disorders are among the most common causes of female infertility. Valid, recommended methods to confirm ovulation: (1) mid-luteal serum progesterone (day 21 of a 28-day cycle, or 7 days before expected menses); a level >3 ng/mL confirms ovulation—this is the most sensitive and practical test; (2) urinary ovulation predictor kits (OPKs) that detect the pre-ovulatory LH surge; (3) basal body temperature (BBT) charting, which shows a rise of about 0.3–0.5 °C after ovulation (progesterone's thermogenic effect)—cheap but retrospective and imprecise; (4) ultrasound monitoring of follicular growth and collaps…

questions.explanation_en: HPV vaccine: a non-live recombinant vaccine protecting against high-risk types (16 and 18, causing most cervical cancers) and wart-causing types (6 and 11). Dosing depends on age at initiation: two doses if started before age 15; three doses if started at ≥15 or in immunocompromised persons. Even with prior exposure or an existing lesion, vaccination is beneficial to cover other types not yet acquired. HPV typing is not a prerequisite for vaccination.

questions.question_fa: دخترخانم17 سالهای به علت درد شدید و زخم در دستگاه تناسلی به درمانگاه مراجعه کرده است. در معاینه بیمار یک زخم حدود 2×2 cm در لبیامینور راست دارد که لمس آن بسیار دردناک میباشد. در معاینه اینگوینال راست لنفادنوپاتی یکطرفه دردناک نیز قابل لمس است. مناسبترین تشخیص کدام است؟
questions.question_en: A 17-year-old girl with severe pain and a 2×2 cm very tender ulcer on the right labium minus, plus painful unilateral right inguinal lymphadenopathy. Most likely diagnosis?

questions.explanation_en: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi, a gram-negative coccobacillus): a cause of genital ulcer presenting with one or more soft, very painful ulcers with a purulent base and ragged edges, plus painful unilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy that may suppurate and rupture. Key distinction: a painful ulcer (chancroid) versus the painless, firm ulcer (syphilitic chancre). Diagnosis is clinical with culture/PCR; treatment is single-dose azithromycin or ceftriaxone, plus screening for other STIs (especially HIV).
